# Was the Ticketmaster outage on Nov 20 a cyberattack?

**Not established.** Ticketmaster has not given a cause, and no source we read says the outage was an attack or rules one out. Nobody has claimed responsibility. The only suggestion of one is an anonymous comment with no evidence.

Incident: Ticketmaster outage, Nov 20, 2026. Also reported as the Ticketmaster outage and Ticketmaster down. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 23, 2026, 8:59 AM ET.

Picture: A printed Ticketmaster ticket. Image: Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ticketmaster_paper_ticket.jpg).

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. ## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Ticketmaster sells tickets nationwide, and fans at shows in New Orleans and Miami could not get in. Reports came from several states and abroad, events in Mexico City were delayed, and the AFL in Australia called the outage global. Ticketmaster has not said how many people were affected.
- Who is affected: People trying to load Ticketmaster tickets on Friday evening, Nov 20 (ET), most visibly at the Caesars Superdome, an arena show in Miami, two events in Mexico City and a football final in Melbourne. Ticketmaster said service was normal by 12:34 AM ET. On Nov 19, entry was held up in Sioux Falls.

### Known so far

- Ticketmaster's service had an outage on Friday night, Nov 20, that kept fans at the Superdome from loading mobile tickets, according to the event organizer and the venue manager.
- Ticketmaster said at 12:34 AM ET on Saturday, Nov 21, that tickets were displaying properly again. It did not say what went wrong.
- On Saturday, Nov 21, Ticketmaster told fans to save tickets to a phone wallet before the second Superdome show and said the problem was fixed. It again gave no cause.
- Ticketmaster failures also delayed entry at a concert and a music festival in Mexico City that night, according to the venue and the promoter.
- On Thursday, Nov 19, a Ticketmaster outage held up entry at the South Dakota state volleyball tournament, according to the tournament's organizer.
- The White House said on Nov 18 that it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind recent tech outages. That was before this outage and does not name Ticketmaster.

### Not known yet

- What caused the outage. Ticketmaster has not said.
- Whether it was a cyberattack. No one has claimed one, reported one, or ruled one out.
- Whether it is linked to the Nov 19 disruption or to other outages this month.
- How many people were affected.
- Whether fans who missed the Nov 20 show will get refunds. WWL asked Ticketmaster and has not reported an answer.

## Related, but separate

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Ticketmaster outage is linked to Thursday's disruption or to this month's other outages | Not established | No source links the Nov 20 outage to the Nov 19 disruption, to Ticketmaster's October transfer problems, or to the FAA, Microsoft 365, bank or other outages of recent weeks. | No source ties the events together or rules it out for Ticketmaster. Hindustan Times mentions the string of outages but offers no link. TicketNews notes the November 12-13 Microsoft outage affected ticket access through email but treats it as separate. Milenio and La Crónica de Hoy note that Telcel's mobile service in Mexico also had problems that Friday, without linking the two. The same company is involved on both nights, which is why we ask. TicketNews's Nov 21 roundup says whether the two nights were related has not been established. ## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the latest update (Nov 23, 9 AM ET).

- A Ticketmaster or Live Nation statement giving the cause of the Nov 20 outage or the Nov 19 disruption. Its Nov 21 all-clear and its Saturday advice to fans give none.
- A Ticketmaster status page or incident notice. We did not find a public one.
- Any vendor, cloud provider or software update named as involved.
- Any claim of responsibility or credible report of a hack.
- Any statement from an official body tying the outage to the week's other outages. The White House's Nov 18 statement predates it and does not name Ticketmaster.
- A count of affected customers.
- A cause for the lines at the Kaseya Center in Miami. WSVN says the company has not confirmed one.
- Most of the Ticketmaster posts on X from during the outage. We relied on how news outlets quote them. We did read Ticketmaster's 12:34 AM ET all-clear directly.
- A statement from Ticketmaster México or the Corona Capital organizers on the cause. Milenio, read directly, says there was no official statement on the cause.
- A cause from Ticketmaster or the AFL for the queues at Ikon Park in Melbourne. Ticketmaster only said it was looking into it.
- A national report of the outage's cause. The Tennessean's USA TODAY Network story, read directly, gives none and says nothing of an attack.
